_policy: POST-CUTOVER BASELINE SEALING. Every successful cutover invalidates the tracked reference it
used, because R(L) == A can only hold while A describes current production.
A_next = R(L_post) is accepted for ONE reason: L_post matched the materialized target that
was just approved. Never because it is live, never because it is newer.
FAIL CLOSED: if the most recent record for a workflow is not SEALED, the next deployment of
that workflow is refused until it is.

sealProof.method: offline rebuild: applyDelta(delta(A,B), A), redacted, compared to R(L_current)

_note: SEALED 2026-08-28, immediately after the P8.4A-R correction: COMMITTED replay is now
idempotently SUCCESSFUL. Delta: +2 nodes (IF Receipt Settled, Internal Result (Committed
Replay)), one modified body (Receipt Read Verdict), one rewire (IF Receipt Claimable false).
WHY: live execution 3791 replayed an already-COMMITTED submission and got SUBMIT_UNRESOLVED
with retryable:true. Safe -- no second write, no corruption -- but not idempotent, and the
retry advice was wrong for a permanently settled submission. After the Concierge migration
that would have meant the lead IS captured while the customer is never confirmed.
SETTLED is a SEPARATE flag from CLAIMABLE on purpose: claiming writes, resolving does not.
Conflating them would have put a Pipeline write on the replay path -- the defect inverted.
COMMITTED without a canonical_lead_id FAILS CLOSED; identity is never inferred from email,
phone or a Pipeline search. The receipt correlation_id is never rewritten and
Pipeline.request_id is never mutated: the original commit correlation stays immutable.
LIVE RE-PROOF: exec 3797 (a1) and 3799 (a2) both returned ok:true with the ORIGINAL
canonical_lead_id, zero Pipeline writes, zero receipt writes. Regression re-checked:
exec 3801 missing-receipt, 3803 IN_FLIGHT, 3805 correlation mismatch -- all unchanged.
The 100-node pre-correction state is frozen at n8n/history/QmIyEW2ZEqKregmN.pre-replay-fix.json.

_note: SEALED 2026-08-28, immediately after WRITE B: the Concierge lead handoff moved from the
PUBLIC Lead Intake webhook to the STRUCTURAL internal Execute Workflow route deployed by
Write A. Delta: +2 nodes (Build Internal Handoff, Send Lead to Intake (Internal)), -1 node
(Send Lead to Intake, the public httpRequest, removed by exact id and exact live edges),
4 rewires, ZERO modified inherited bodies.
THE KEY IS NOT MINTED AT HANDOFF. Build Internal Handoff reads the submission_key from
Issuance Gate -- the same node Receipt Preallocate writes the receipt with -- so the handoff
carries the authoritative key the cycle already owns. A second mint would orphan that receipt.
Issuance Gate is used rather than Issuance Verdict because Verdict only runs when a
preallocation was required; on the REUSE path it never executes.
TWO MATERIALIZER GAPS WERE CLOSED to make this deployable, both found by this battery:
approvedAddedNodes approved a node by NAME and left its PARAMETERS unconstrained, so the
Execute Workflow target could be repointed or made a caller-steerable expression and the
handoff body could take the key from the request or mint one -- all inside approved names.
And an approvedRemovals entry was only a PERMISSION: a candidate that simply kept the public
HTTP node produced no delta op and nothing objected, which would have deployed BOTH paths.
The 50-node pre-Write-B state is frozen at n8n/history/mppzthlkSJFr6Kle.pre-write-b.json.
LIVE END-TO-END TELEGRAM PROOF IS NOT PART OF THIS SEAL: it requires a real Telegram cycle
driven by the owner. The seal asserts only that production equals the approved target.
